minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 8, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on December 8, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 3, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager /Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of Subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9. State Water Resources Control Board Administration Appeal
  (MS-4 permit)

City Council Minutes  1  December 8, 2015
 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation. Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (5
  potential cases): Funding /site remediation issues related to slope failure issues

CS3. Matters Posing Threats to Public Services or Facilities: Consultation with City Police
  Chief\Orange County Sheriffs and City Attorney GC 54957

CS4. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:09
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced agenda items CS1 and CS2 were variance of litigation matters.
The Council received updates, gave direction and staff will proceed accordingly. Item CS3 was a
general overview of security issues. Lt. NewMyer and support staff will be giving the public good
information for dealing with community crisis matters and there was no further reportable
action. Mr. Curley announced that agenda item CS4 was a personnel matter and no reportable
action occurred.

*Note: City Attorney Curley asked the Council to consider reordering the agenda to consider item
17 earlier. The applicant is requesting a 60-90 day extension and if the Council Members so desire,
they can open the public hearing, continue it and therefore allow several members of the audience
and staff to go home.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

Item 17 was taken out of order.

PUBLIC HEARING

17.  Appeal filed by Ryan Farsai of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s
  approval of Conditional Use Permit CUP2015-343, Minor Modification MM2015-
  354, and Variance VAR2015-44, petitions submitted by Ryan Farsai to permit the
  renovation of an existing Arco gas station located at 25122 Marguerite Parkway, in
  the CC (Commercial Community) zone. CUP2015-343 is filed for expansion of the
  existing convenience store and for a Type 21 Alcohol Beverage Control (ABC) license

City Council Minutes  2  December 8, 2015
   allowing off-sales of beer, wine and distilled spirits. MM2015-354 is filed for site
  improvements including revised parking and landscape, and exterior building
  improvements including the expanded convenience store and a new smog-test bay, all
  with an updated architectural theme. VAR2015-44 is filed for reduced building
  setbacks along the site frontage with Marguerite Parkway and La Paz Road

  City Attorney Curley noted that the applicant, Ryan Farsai, has requested a 60-90 day
  extension on his appeal.

  Mayor Schlicht opened the public hearing. Upon finding no requests to speak, she closed
  the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  continue the item for 90 days at the request of the applicant (March 8, 2016.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Bill Cook as a Hometown Hero

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Bill Cook.

P2.  Mayor’s State of the City Address

  Mayor Schlicht presented her State of the City video.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Helen Workun, M.V.: representing the scholarship committee of the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee, Ms. Workun announced that the deadline for scholarship applications has been
extended until the end of February. Applications are available at mvactivities.com and she
encouraged eligible high school seniors to apply.

Jim Leach, Santa Margarita Water District: thanked the City for its continued leadership in water
conservation and use reduction. He announced that notices have been sent to homeowners
regarding the new rate structure and SMWD is hosting a series of open houses where residents can
learn more about the new rates. The first open house is this evening at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray
Community Center in Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  3  December 8, 2015
 Chuck McCollough, President of the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce, M.V.: announced that
the Chamber will be hosting its signature Christmas Mixer at the Murray Community Center and
all proceeds will be donated to Age Well Senior Services. Attendees should bring a gift of $25 as
a donation and he invited the Council Members to attend. Mr. McCollough also announced that
the Chamber's weekly networking event will be held at High Park Taphouse.

Jake Vollebregt, Aliso Viejo: on behalf of the Board of Directors of the South Orange
County Economic Coalition, he announced that they are hosting the 2016 Economic Report at
Saddleback College on Feb 5, 2016, at 11:30 a.m. The goal is to facilitate collaboration between
government, business and community leaders and he invited the Council Members and staff to
participate.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of November 10, 2015,
  as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated October 30, 2015 in the Amount of $591,996.04

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated November 6, 2015 in the Amount of $2,237,576.70

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  4  December 8, 2015
 6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2015

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2015

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  September  2015

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for September 2015

  Received and filed.

10.  Annual Measure M-2 Expenditure Report for Fiscal Year Ended June 30,
  2015

  Approved Resolution 15-60 Adopting the Measure M2 Expenditure Report for the City of
  Mission Viejo.

11.  Federal Transportation Improvement Program

  Adopted Resolution 15-61 Certifying that the City of Mission Viejo Has the Resources to
  Fund the Projects in the FFY 2016/17-2021/22 Transportation Improvement Program and
  Affirming Its Commitment to Implement All Projects in the Program.

12.  Renewal of Library Automated System Software and Hardware Support Agreement

  Approved issuance of a purchase order for year 4 of 5 year agreement in the amount of
  $65,437.41 for maintenance and support of the Library Automated Systems (ALS)
  Software and Hardware Agreement with SirsiDynix, Inc.

13.  Library Holiday Schedule for 2016 Calendar Year

  Approved proposed Library Holiday and Closure Schedule for 2016.

14.  Contract Amendment - John Deere Landscapes, Inc. Name Change

City Council Minutes  5  December 8, 2015
   Approved First Amendment to John Deere Landscapes, Inc. agreement to reflect the
  change of the company's name to SiteOne Landscape Supply.

15.  Oso Parkway Widening, 5 Freeway to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)-Notice of
  Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

16.  Safety Lighting LED Conversions (CIP 228)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for Safety Lighting LED Conversions to Express
  Energy Services, Inc., in the amount of $86,944 (A15-60); and (2) authorized staff to issue
  a purchase order to Express Energy Services, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $41,884
  ($45,060 in rebates/incentives to be collected by Express Energy Services directly from
  Southern California Edison).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  Check Register Dated November 13, 2015 in the Amount of $1,682,262.61

  Mayor Schlicht asked about a payment to Kosmont and Associates for September
  Economic Development advisory services in the amount of $3,000. She asked if the City
  is on a monthly contract and will there be reports.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that the City has an ongoing contract with Kosmont to
  provide Economic Development services. It is not a flat monthly rate but they bill for
  services performed. In the recent past they have set up and attended a number of meetings
  with business owners across the street from city hall and have been very active in engaging
  property and business owners in terms of the Economic Development goals that the City
  Council has established.

  Mayor Schlicht asked Mayor Pro Tem Raths and Council Member Sachs to begin
  providing regular updates on the Economic Development Committee's activities so the
  Council and public are kept informed.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  6  December 8, 2015
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

18.  Retiree Healthcare Plan June 30, 2015 Actuarial Valuation

  Actuary, John Bartel, Bartel and Associates, presented information on the Retiree
  Healthcare Plan unfunded liability.

19.  Update on Internet Services for the Village Shopping Center (Center)

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander presented the staff report and
  informed that Council that Cox Communications has agreed to establish high-speed
  internet access for the property and business owners, beginning sometime in January
  2016.

NEW BUSINESS

20.  "No Stopping Anytime" Restriction on Entidad at Empanada

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 15-62 to Install "No Stopping Anytime" Parking Restrictions on the North
  Side of Entidad at its Intersection with Empanada to 127 Feet East; and (2) introduce
  Ordinance 15-308 Amending Mission Viejo Municipal Code Chapter 12.08 Relating to
  City Director Authority to Establish Parking and Stopping Restrictions on City
  Highways.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

21.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA)

City Council Minutes  7  December 8, 2015
   Council Member Sachs presented the report.

22.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.

23.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

24.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

25.  PACE Ad Hoc Committee

  City Attorney Curley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

26.  Resolutions Consenting to Inclusion of the City of Mission Viejo Properties in the
  California Home Finance Authority PACE Programs and Associate Membership in
  California Home Finance Authority

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Emily Goodwin and Brent Neben, Ygrene: presented an overview of the California Home
  Finance Authority Ygrene program.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 15-63 Consenting to Inclusion of Properties Within the City's
  Incorporated Area in CHF Community Facilities District No. 2014-1 (Clean Energy) to
  Finance Renewable Energy Generation, Energy Efficiency, Water Conservation and
  Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Improvements and Approving Associate
  membership in CHF, and (2) adopt Resolution 15-64 Consenting to Inclusion of
  Properties within the City's Incorporated Area in the CHF PACE Program to Finance
  Renewable Energy Generation, Energy and Water Efficiency Improvements and Electric
  Vehicle Charging Infrastructure and Approving Associate Membership in CHF.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  8  December 8, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

27.  An Urgency Ordinance of the City of Mission Viejo, California adding Chapter
  11.23 in Title 11 of Mission Viejo Municipal Code to Prohibit Marijuana
  Dispensaries, Marijuana Cultivation, Marijuana Delivery and Related
  Transportation within the City Boundaries and to ensure prosecutorial and
  jurisdictional provisions to the City or State, as Respectively Required

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to adopt
  Urgency Ordinance 15-309.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:16 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:30
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg reported that staff received a series of questions from the City of Laguna
Hills pertaining to the operations of the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center. He provided the
Council Members with a copy of staff's letter which responds to the Laguna Hills inquiries.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

28.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Council Minutes  9  December 8, 2015
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including the City’s Veterans
Day ceremony, the Marine Corps ball, and Orange County Business Council’s 5th annual “Turning
Red Tape Into Red Carpet” awards, one of which Mission Viejo was nominated for. She also
attended the Mission Viejo Activities Committee (MVAC) Gifts and Goodies Boutique and she
encouraged parents to look into the scholarships that are being offered through the
MVAC. Council Member Bucknum attended Assemblyman Bill Brough's open house and she
thanked him for attending tonight’s Council meeting. She also congratulated Congresswoman
Mimi Walters for presiding over the floor today. Council Member Bucknum announced that the
Mission Viejo High School Diablos football team won the CIF division and are heading to the
State Championships. The first game will be held Friday, December 11 at Mission Viejo High
School. She noted that tickets went on sale today and will also be sold tomorrow from 5:00 to 6:30
p.m. at the high school ticket booth. Council Member Bucknum asked staff to report, at a future
meeting, on the home improvement permit process and if the City has an online system to track
permit status. She encouraged residents to look at the Orange County Sheriff’s Department “Run,
Hide and Fight” program which talks about surviving an active shooter event. Council Member
Bucknum shared 5 tips for a happy holiday season and stated that it has been an absolute honor to
serve on the City Council this year. In closing, she asked the Mayor to adjourn the meeting in
memory of the San Bernardino terrorist massacre victims.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs joked that he didn't recognize that a year has gone by until Facebook
reminded him with photos from one year ago. He stated that this year, serving on the City Council,
has been exciting, wonderful and fun. He noted that new Council Members often come in thinking
they know everything and that they’re going to change things but it doesn't take long to realize that
they have a lot to learn. He stated that things that are no-brainers in the business world can take a
long time to get done in government. Council Member Sachs stated that he is trying to become
someone who listens more than talks and he is working on it and getting much better. He said that
serving on the Council has been a learning experience and serving on regional committees and
boards has been a wealth of knowledge and he is thankful for that. In closing, Council Member
Sachs wished the community a happy Hanukkah, Merry Christmas and a happy, healthy New Year.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury noted that both this City Council and OCTA have given direction to staff to
work on El Nino abatement. In the past week or two there was a small fire on the ravine off La
Paz near the railroad track. When the fire was over, some residents who cut down trees left them
there and he thanked City staff for working with OCTA staff so professionally and quickly to clear
the area. Council Member Ury stated that the Santa’s arrival event was a lot of fun and he noted
that there was a bigger turn out than ever before. He also thanked Mayor Schlicht for the time and

City Council Minutes  10  December 8, 2015
 effort she has put into the role of Mayor and in closing, Council Member Ury wished everyone a
Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukkah and a great holiday season.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths notified the City Manager that he is getting a lot of phone calls and emails
regarding the Oso Parkway single-entry freeway onramp and he asked if staff can look into getting
a two-lane entry. He read a prepared statement regarding his service on the Council this year and
he thanked his colleagues for their trust and confidence in appointing him to serve as Mayor Pro
Tem. He stated that he looks forward to continuing to serve in a leadership role and he thanked
the City Manager and Assistant City Manager for their dedication in keeping staff working
smoothly and effectively. Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked his colleagues for passing responsible
legislation and for their dedication to serve the City and he stated that now is not the time to take
a breath; the City Council needs to move forward with fresh, new leadership as was mandated by
the citizens who voted for three new Council Members in the last election. In conclusion, Mayor
Pro Tem Raths thanked the community for their support and confidence and he wished everyone
a Merry Christmas.

Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht stated that she would like to give an assignment to the Community Services
Commission to coordinate volunteer services for residents who are in distress and needing help
with minor household repairs or yard work. She noted that she received a request from Pastor
Mike who is looking for a way to reach out to the community so she thought the best place to start
would be through the Community Services Commission. Mayor Schlicht asked the City Attorney
to provide direction on getting a survey of customer satisfaction concerns regarding building
permit services sent directly to the Council and not through staff. She discussed a City of Laguna
Niguel Police Services flier that has tips on preparing for El Nino and interesting information about
panhandler loitering. Mayor Schlicht discussed her attendance at the Mission Viejo High School
Diablos football game where they won against Murietta and she said that she was happy to see that
Fox News West gave kudos to notable Mission Viejo High School graduate athletes. She also
announced that the Saddleback College Gauchos football team championship game will be
streamed on the Internet. Circling back to the subject of El Nino, Mayor Schlicht reminded
residents to consider getting flood insurance and noted that the California Department of Insurance
recommends the same and she will provide information for the public record. In honor of Pearl
Harbor Day, December 7, she shared the quote: “Remember Pearl Harbor, keep America
alert.” Mayor Schlicht stated that Americans were reminded last week that we are still at war and
she expressed her condolences for those slain and injured in the San Bernardino shooting. She
also expressed gratitude to first responders who went into the fight without thinking of
themselves. In closing, Mayor Schlicht wished the community a happy Hanukkah, Merry
Christmas, and happy New Year. She said that despite the Council Member’s snipping and

City Council Minutes  11  December 8, 2015
 disparaging remarks, they did find a way to balance their differences and put the citizens first. She
expressed thanks to her colleagues for their hard work in 2015.

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

29.  Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2016

  Assemblyman Bill Brough: thanked Cathy Schlicht for her service as Mayor this year and
  presented her with a Certificate of Recognition on behalf of the California Legislature.
  City Clerk Karen Hamman asked the Council Members to make nominations for Mayor
  and Mayor Pro Tem for 2016.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to appoint
  Frank Ury to serve as Mayor in 2016.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  appoint Greg Raths to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2016. Mr. Raths declined the
  appointment so the nomination was withdrawn.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to appoint Ed
  Sachs to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2016. Mr. Sachs declined the appointment so the
  nomination was withdrawn.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Ury, to appoint
  Wendy Bucknum to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2016.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  12  December 8, 2015
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:59 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting in memory of the victims of the San Bernardino terrorist
massacre, to Tuesday, January 12, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 12, 2016

City Council Minutes  13  December 8, 2015
